sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tulyaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ adhārmikās tu hantavyā ity ahaṃ prabravīmi vaḥ
english: "I am indeed impartial to all beings—of this there is no doubt; yet the unrighteous must be slain: thus do I declare to you.

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ sthāṇum īśānaṃ jiṣṇum akliṣṭakāriṇam yoddhāraṃ vṛṇutādityāḥ sa tān hantā suretarān
english: Choose, then, O Ādityas, as your warrior Sthāṇu, the Lord Īśāna, the ever-victorious, who acts without weariness; he shall slay those foes of the gods."

sanskrit: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ brahmāṇam agrataḥ kṛtvā vṛṣāṅkaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
english: Hearing this his word, the gods, with Śakra at their head, placed Brahmā before them and went for refuge to him whose emblem is the bull.

sanskrit: tapaḥ paraṃ samātasthur gṛṇanto brahma śāśvatam ṛṣibhiḥ saha dharmajñā bhavaṃ sarvātmanā gatāḥ
english: They undertook the highest austerity, chanting the eternal Brahman; and those knowers of dharma, together with the sages, drew near to Bhava with their whole being.

sanskrit: tuṣṭuvur vāgbhir arthyābhir bhayeṣv abhayakṛttamam sarvātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ yenāptaṃ sarvam ātmanā
english: With meaningful words they praised him who, in terrors, grants safety best of all—the All-Self, the great-souled one, by whom the whole was pervaded through his own being,

sanskrit: tapoviśeṣair bahubhir yogaṃ yo veda cātmanaḥ yaḥ sāṃkhyam ātmano veda yasya cātmā vaśe sadā
english: who by many special austerities knows the yoga of the self, who knows the Sāṃkhya of the self, and whose self is ever under his own command.

sanskrit: te taṃ dadṛśur īśānaṃ tejorāśim umāpatim ananyasadṛśaṃ loke vratavantam akalmaṣam
english: They beheld that Īśāna, a mass of splendor, the lord of Umā, who in the world is like none other, steadfast in vows, untouched by stain.

sanskrit: ekaṃ ca bhagavantaṃ te nānārūpam akalpayan ātmanaḥ pratirūpāṇi rūpāṇy atha mahātmani parasparasya cāpaśyan sarve paramavismitāḥ
english: And they perceived the one Blessed Lord as manifold in form; in that great-souled one they saw forms that were reflections of their own selves, and they beheld one another there, all of them utterly amazed.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtamayaṃ ceśaṃ tam ajaṃ jagataḥ patim devā brahmarṣayaś caiva śirobhir dharaṇīṃ gatāḥ
english: And the gods and the brahmin-sages bowed their heads to the earth before that Lord who is made of all beings, the unborn, the master of the world.

sanskrit: tān svastivākyenābhyarcya samutthāpya ca śaṃkaraḥ brūta brūteti bhagavān smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Honoring them with a word of blessing and raising them up, Śaṃkara the Blessed One, smiling, addressed them: "Speak, speak."

sanskrit: tryambakeṇābhyanujñātās tatas te 'svasthacetasaḥ namo namas te 'stu vibho tata ity abruvan bhavam
english: Granted leave by the Three-Eyed One, then, though their minds were still unsettled, they said to Bhava: "Homage, homage be to you, O all-pervading Lord!"

sanskrit: namo devātidevāya dhanvine cātimanyave prajāpatimakhaghnāya prajāpatibhir īḍyase
english: "Homage to the God beyond the gods, the bearer of the bow, the surpassingly wrathful; you who destroyed the sacrifice of Prajāpati, you are extolled by the Prajāpatis.

sanskrit: namaḥ stutāya stutyāya stūyamānāya mṛtyave vilohitāya rudrāya nīlagrīvāya śūline
english: Homage to him who is praised, who is worthy of praise, who is being praised, to Death itself; to the deep-red Rudra, the blue-throated, the wielder of the trident.

sanskrit: amoghāya mṛgākṣāya pravarāyudhayodhine durvāraṇāya śukrāya brahmaṇe brahmacāriṇe
english: To the unerring, the deer-eyed, the fighter with the choicest weapons; to the irresistible, the radiant, to Brahman, to the keeper of chastity.

sanskrit: īśānāyāprameyāya niyantre carmavāsase taponityāya piṅgāya vratine kṛttivāsase
english: To Īśāna, the immeasurable, the restrainer, clad in a hide; to him constant in austerity, the tawny-hued, the keeper of vows, robed in a skin.

sanskrit: kumārapitre tryakṣāya pravarāyudhadhāriṇe prapannārtivināśāya brahmadviṭsaṃghaghātine
english: To the father of Kumāra, the three-eyed, the bearer of the choicest weapons; to the destroyer of the suffering of those who take refuge, the slayer of the hosts of Brahman's haters.

sanskrit: vanaspatīnāṃ pataye narāṇāṃ pataye namaḥ gavāṃ ca pataye nityaṃ yajñānāṃ pataye namaḥ
english: Homage to the lord of the forest-trees, to the lord of men; and ever homage to the lord of cattle, to the lord of sacrifices.

sanskrit: namo 'stu te sasainyāya tryambakāyogratejase manovākkarmabhir deva tvāṃ prapannān bhajasva naḥ
english: Homage be to you with your hosts, to the Three-Eyed One of fierce splendor; O God, accept us who have taken refuge in you by thought, word, and deed."

sanskrit: tataḥ prasanno bhagavān svāgatenābhinandya tān provāca vyetu vastrāso brūta kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ
english: Then the Blessed One, well pleased, greeted them with a welcome and said: "Let your fear depart; tell me, what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: pitṛdevarṣisaṃghebhyo vare datte mahātmanā satkṛtya śaṃkaraṃ prāha brahmā lokahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: When the great-souled one had granted his boon to the hosts of fathers, gods, and sages, Brahmā, doing honor to Śaṃkara, spoke a word for the world's welfare:

sanskrit: tavātisargād deveśa prājāpatyam idaṃ padam mayādhitiṣṭhatā datto dānavebhyo mahān varaḥ
english: "By your bestowal, O Lord of the gods, I hold this office of Prajāpati; and while presiding over it I have granted a great boon to the Dānavas.

sanskrit: tān atikrāntamaryādān nānyaḥ saṃhartum arhati tvām ṛte bhūtabhavyeśa tvaṃ hy eṣāṃ pratyarir vadhe
english: None but you, O Lord of what is and what shall be, is able to destroy them, who have overstepped all bounds; for you alone are their match in slaying them.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ deva prapannānāṃ yācatāṃ ca divaukasām kuru prasādaṃ deveśa dānavāñ jahi śūlabhṛt
english: Therefore, O God, to these dwellers in heaven who have taken refuge and now entreat you, show your grace, O Lord of the gods, and slay the Dānavas, O bearer of the trident."

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca hantavyāḥ śatravaḥ sarve yuṣmākam iti me matiḥ na tv eko 'haṃ vadhe teṣāṃ samartho vai suradviṣām
english: The Blessed Lord said: "That all your foes must be slain—such is my own resolve; yet I alone am not equal to the slaying of those haters of the gods.

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ sahitāḥ sarve madīyenāstratejasā jayadhvaṃ yudhi tāñ śatrūn saṃghāto hi mahābalaḥ
english: Do you, then, all united, by the power of my weapon conquer those enemies in battle; for union is a mighty strength."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ asmattejobalaṃ yāvat tāvad dviguṇam eva ca teṣām iti ha manyāmo dṛṣṭatejobalā hi te
english: The gods said: "Whatever is the measure of our splendor and strength, theirs is twice as much—so we judge, for we have seen their splendor and strength."

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca vadhyās te sarvataḥ pāpā ye yuṣmāsv aparādhinaḥ mama tejobalārdhena sarvāṃs tān ghnata śātravān
english: The Blessed One said: "Those evil ones who have wronged you must by all means be slain; with half my splendor and strength, smite all those foes."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ bibhartuṃ tejaso 'rdhaṃ te na śakṣyāmo maheśvara sarveṣāṃ no balārdhena tvam eva jahi śātravān
english: The gods said: "We shall not be able to bear half of your splendor, O Maheśvara; rather, with half the strength of us all, do you yourself slay the foes."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca tatas tatheti deveśas tair ukto rājasattama ardham ādāya sarvebhyas tejasābhyadhiko 'bhavat
english: Duryodhana said: Then the Lord of the gods, thus addressed by them, said "So be it," O best of kings; and taking half from them all, he grew yet more abundant in splendor.

sanskrit: sa tu devo balenāsīt sarvebhyo balavattaraḥ mahādeva iti khyātas tadāprabhṛti śaṃkaraḥ
english: And that god became in strength mightier than them all; from that time onward Śaṃkara has been renowned as Mahādeva, the Great God.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahādevo dhanur bāṇadharas tv aham haniṣyāmi rathenājau tān ripūn vai divaukasaḥ
english: Then Mahādeva said: "Bearing bow and arrow, I shall slay in battle those foes from a chariot, O dwellers in heaven.

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ me rathaṃ caiva dhanur bāṇaṃ tathaiva ca paśyadhvaṃ yāvad adyaitān pātayāmi mahītale
english: Do you, then, look to my chariot and likewise to my bow and arrow, while this day I lay them low upon the earth."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ mūrtisarvasvam ādāya trailokyasya tatas tataḥ rathaṃ te kalpayiṣyāma deveśvara mahaujasam
english: The gods said: "Taking the whole substance of the three worlds from every side, we shall fashion for you, O Lord of gods, a chariot of mighty might."

sanskrit: tathaiva buddhyā vihitaṃ viśvakarmakṛtaṃ śubham tato vibudhaśārdūlās taṃ rathaṃ samakalpayan
english: Thus, devised by their intelligence, wrought by Viśvakarman and auspicious, those tigers among the gods then fashioned that chariot.

sanskrit: vandhuraṃ pṛthivīṃ devīṃ viśālapuramālinīm saparvatavanadvīpāṃ cakrur bhūtadharāṃ tadā
english: For its frame they made the goddess Earth, garlanded with broad cities, bearing her mountains, forests, and islands, the upholder of beings.

sanskrit: mandaraṃ parvataṃ cākṣaṃ jaṅghās tasya mahānadīḥ diśaś ca pradiśaś caiva parivāraṃ rathasya hi
english: Mount Mandara they made its axle, the great rivers its struts, and the quarters and intermediate quarters the encircling rim of the chariot.

sanskrit: anukarṣān grahān dīptān varūthaṃ cāpi tārakāḥ dharmārthakāmasaṃyuktaṃ triveṇuṃ cāpi bandhuram oṣadhīr vividhās tatra nānāpuṣpaphalodgamāḥ
english: The blazing planets they made its underbeams, and the stars its guard-rail; the threefold pole, joined to dharma, artha, and kāma, they made its binding, and the manifold herbs, with their varied burst of flowers and fruits, were set therein.

sanskrit: sūryācandramasau kṛtvā cakre rathavarottame pakṣau pūrvāparau tatra kṛte rātryahanī śubhe
english: Making the sun and moon the two wheels of that best of chariots, they set there as its front and rear flanks the auspicious night and day.

sanskrit: daśa nāgapatīn īṣāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭramukhān dṛḍhām dyāṃ yugaṃ yugacarmāṇi saṃvartakabalāhakān
english: The ten lords of serpents, headed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, they made its sturdy shaft; the sky its yoke, and the world-dissolving clouds the yoke-straps.

sanskrit: śamyāṃ dhṛtiṃ ca medhāṃ ca sthitiṃ saṃnatim eva ca grahanakṣatratārābhiś carma citraṃ nabhastalam
english: Firmness, wisdom, steadiness, and humility they made its yoke-pins; and the vault of heaven, with its planets, lunar mansions, and stars, became the dappled covering.

sanskrit: surāmbupretavittānāṃ patīṃl lokeśvarān hayān sinīvālīm anumatiṃ kuhūṃ rākāṃ ca suvratām yoktrāṇi cakrur vāhānāṃ rohakāṃś cāpi kaṇṭhakam
english: The lords of the worlds—the masters of the gods, the waters, the spirits, and wealth—they made its horses; and Sinīvālī, Anumati, Kuhū, and the devout Rākā they made the harness-ropes of the steeds, and the cross-bars too, and the throat-strap.

sanskrit: karma satyaṃ tapo 'rthaś ca vihitās tatra raśmayaḥ adhiṣṭhānaṃ manas tv āsīt parirathyaṃ sarasvatī
english: Action, truth, austerity, and gain were set there as the reins; the mind became the standing-place, and Sarasvatī the surrounding road.

sanskrit: nānāvarṇāś ca citrāś ca patākāḥ pavaneritāḥ vidyudindradhanurnaddhaṃ rathaṃ dīptaṃ vyadīpayat
english: Banners of many hues and varied design, stirred by the wind, and the lightning bound to it as Indra's bow, made the blazing chariot blaze the more.

sanskrit: evaṃ tasmin mahārāja kalpite rathasattame devair manujaśārdūla dviṣatām abhimardane
english: When that best of chariots had thus been fashioned, O great king, by the gods, O tiger among men, for the crushing of the foes,

sanskrit: svāny āyudhāni mukhyāni nyadadhāc chaṃkaro rathe rathayaṣṭiṃ viyatkṛṣṭāṃ sthāpayām āsa govṛṣam
english: Śaṃkara laid his own chief weapons upon the chariot, and set up the bull as its banner-staff, drawn out across the sky.

sanskrit: brahmadaṇḍaḥ kāladaṇḍo rudradaṇḍas tathā jvaraḥ pariskandā rathasyāsya sarvatodiśam udyatāḥ
english: The rod of Brahman, the rod of Time, the rod of Rudra, and Fever stood ready as the outriders of that chariot, raised on every side.

sanskrit: atharvāṅgirasāv āstāṃ cakrarakṣau mahātmanaḥ ṛgvedaḥ sāmavedaś ca purāṇaṃ ca puraḥsarāḥ
english: The Atharvan and the Aṅgiras hymns became the wheel-guards of the great-souled one; the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Purāṇa went before him.

sanskrit: itihāsayajurvedau pṛṣṭharakṣau babhūvatuḥ divyā vācaś ca vidyāś ca paripārśvacarāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: The lore of old and the Yajurveda became his rear-guards; and the divine speeches and the sacred sciences were made to attend at his flanks.

sanskrit: tottrādayaś ca rājendra vaṣaṭkāras tathaiva ca oṃkāraś ca mukhe rājann atiśobhākaro 'bhavat
english: The goad and the rest, O lord of kings, and the cry of Vaṣaṭ likewise, and at its front the syllable Oṃ, O king, became a maker of surpassing splendor.

sanskrit: vicitram ṛtubhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ kṛtvā saṃvatsaraṃ dhanuḥ tasmān nṝṇāṃ kālarātrir jyā kṛtā dhanuṣo 'jarā
english: Making the year, dappled with its six seasons, into the bow, and the Night of Time, the doom of men, into the bow's unaging string—

sanskrit: iṣuś cāpy abhavad viṣṇur jvalanaḥ soma eva ca agnīṣomau jagat kṛtsnaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ cocyate jagat
english: And the arrow became Viṣṇu, blazing fire and Soma alike; for Agni and Soma are the whole world, and the world is called Viṣṇu's own.

sanskrit: viṣṇuś cātmā bhagavato bhavasyāmitatejasaḥ tasmād dhanurjyāsaṃsparśaṃ na viṣehur harasya te
english: And Viṣṇu is the very self of the Blessed Bhava of measureless splendor; therefore those foes could not endure the touch of Hara's bowstring.

sanskrit: tasmiñ śare tigmamanyur mumocāviṣahaṃ prabhuḥ bhṛgvaṅgiromanyubhavaṃ krodhāgnim atiduḥsaham
english: Into that arrow the Lord, his wrath made keen, loosed an unbearable fire of anger, born of the fury of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, exceedingly hard to withstand.

sanskrit: sa nīlalohito dhūmraḥ kṛttivāsā bhayaṃkaraḥ ādityāyutasaṃkāśas tejojvālāvṛto jvalan
english: Dark-blue and red, smoke-hued, clad in a hide, terrible to behold, like ten thousand suns, wrapped in flames of splendor, he blazed.

sanskrit: duścyāvaś cyāvano jetā hantā brahmadviṣāṃ haraḥ nityaṃ trātā ca hantā ca dharmādharmāśritāñ janān
english: Hard to shake, the overthrower, the conqueror, the slayer of Brahman's haters is Hara; ever the protector and the destroyer of folk according as they cleave to dharma or to its opposite.

sanskrit: pramāthibhir ghorarūpair bhīmodagrair gaṇair vṛtaḥ vibhāti bhagavān sthāṇus tair evātmaguṇair vṛtaḥ
english: Surrounded by his tormenting hosts, dread of form, fierce and towering, the Blessed Sthāṇu shone forth, encompassed by those very qualities of his own self.

sanskrit: tasyāṅgāni samāśritya sthitaṃ viśvam idaṃ jagat jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ rājañ śuśubhe 'dbhutadarśanam
english: Resting upon his limbs stood this whole universe, moving and unmoving, O king, and it shone, a wondrous sight to see.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu taṃ rathaṃ divyaṃ kavacī sa śarāsanī bāṇam ādatta taṃ divyaṃ somaviṣṇvagnisaṃbhavam
english: Beholding that divine chariot, mailed and bow in hand, he took up that divine arrow sprung from Soma, Viṣṇu, and Agni.

sanskrit: tasya vājāṃs tato devāḥ kalpayāṃ cakrire vibhoḥ puṇyagandhavahaṃ rājañ śvasanaṃ rājasattama
english: Then the gods fashioned for the all-pervading Lord the feathers of that arrow, O king, and the bearer of holy fragrance, the wind, O best of kings, to speed it.

sanskrit: tam āsthāya mahādevas trāsayan daivatāny api āruroha tadā yattaḥ kampayann iva rodasī
english: Mounting it, Mahādeva, terrifying even the gods, then ascended, intent, as though making heaven and earth to tremble.

sanskrit: sa śobhamāno varadaḥ khaḍgī bāṇī śarāsanī hasann ivābravīd devo sārathiḥ ko bhaviṣyati
english: Resplendent, the boon-giver, sword in hand, with arrow and bow, the God said, as if smiling: "Who shall be my charioteer?"

sanskrit: tam abruvan devagaṇā yaṃ bhavān saṃniyokṣyate sa bhaviṣyati deveśa sārathis te na saṃśayaḥ
english: The hosts of gods said to him: "Whomever you shall appoint, O Lord of gods, he shall be your charioteer—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tān abravīt punar devo mattaḥ śreṣṭhataro hi yaḥ taṃ sārathiṃ kurudhvaṃ me svayaṃ saṃcintya māciram
english: The God said to them again: "Whoever is greater than I—make him my charioteer; consider this yourselves, and do not delay."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tato devā vākyam uktaṃ mahātmanā gatvā pitāmahaṃ devaṃ prasādyaivaṃ vaco 'bruvan
english: Hearing this word spoken by the great-souled one, the gods then went to the God, the Grandsire, and propitiating him, spoke thus:

sanskrit: deva tvayedaṃ kathitaṃ tridaśārinibarhaṇam tathā ca kṛtam asmābhiḥ prasanno vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
english: "O God, by you was this destruction of the gods' foes ordained, and so we have done it; and he whose banner is the bull is well pleased.

sanskrit: rathaś ca vihito 'smābhir vicitrāyudhasaṃvṛtaḥ sārathiṃ tu na jānīmaḥ kaḥ syāt tasmin rathottame
english: And the chariot, decked with wondrous weapons, has been arrayed by us; but we know not who should be the charioteer upon that best of chariots.

sanskrit: tasmād vidhīyatāṃ kaś cit sārathir devasattama saphalāṃ tāṃ giraṃ deva kartum arhasi no vibho
english: Therefore let some charioteer be appointed, O best of gods; you ought, O Lord, to make that word of ours bear fruit.

sanskrit: evam asmāsu hi purā bhagavann uktavān asi hitaṃ kartāsmi bhavatām iti tat kartum arhasi
english: For of old, O Blessed One, you said to us, 'I shall do you good'; that you ought now to do.

sanskrit: sa deva yukto rathasattamo no; durāvaro drāvaṇaḥ śātravāṇām pinākapāṇir vihito 'tra yoddhā; vibhīṣayan dānavān udyato 'sau
english: That best of chariots of ours is yoked, O God, hard to oppose, the router of the foes; and there as warrior is stationed the bearer of the Pināka, who, rousing himself, strikes terror into the Dānavas.

sanskrit: tathaiva vedāś caturo hayāgryā; dharā saśailā ca ratho mahātman nakṣatravaṃśo 'nugato varūthe; yasmin yoddhā sārathinābhirakṣyaḥ
english: Even so are the four Vedas his foremost steeds, and the earth with her mountains the chariot, O great-souled one; the train of the lunar mansions follows in the guard-rail—the warrior in which must be protected by a charioteer.

sanskrit: tatra sārathir eṣṭavyaḥ sarvair etair viśeṣavān tatpratiṣṭho ratho deva hayā yoddhā tathaiva ca kavacāni ca śastrāṇi kārmukaṃ ca pitāmaha
english: For that a charioteer must be sought, surpassing all these; upon him rest the chariot, O God, the horses and the warrior alike, the coats of mail, the weapons, and the bow, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: tvām ṛte sārathiṃ tatra nānyaṃ paśyāmahe vayam tvaṃ hi sarvair guṇair yukto devatābhyo 'dhikaḥ prabho sārathye tūrṇam āroha saṃyaccha paramān hayān
english: Save you, we see no other for the charioteer there; for you are endowed with all virtues and surpass the gods, O Lord. Mount swiftly to the charioteer's seat and curb these matchless steeds."

sanskrit: iti te śirasā natvā trilokeśaṃ pitāmaham devāḥ prasādayām āsuḥ sārathyāyeti naḥ śrutam
english: Thus, bowing their heads to the Grandsire, the lord of the three worlds, the gods entreated him for the office of charioteer—so we have heard.

sanskrit: brahmovāca nātra kiṃ cin mṛṣā vākyaṃ yad uktaṃ vo divaukasaḥ saṃyacchāmi hayān eṣa yudhyato vai kapardinaḥ
english: Brahmā said: "In nothing of this is the word you have spoken false, O dwellers in heaven; lo, I shall curb the horses of the matted-haired one as he fights."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān devo lokasraṣṭā pitāmahaḥ sārathye kalpito devair īśānasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then that Blessed God, the Grandsire, the maker of the worlds, was appointed by the gods as charioteer of the great-souled Īśāna.

sanskrit: tasminn ārohati kṣipraṃ syandanaṃ lokapūjite śirobhir agamaṃs tūrṇaṃ te hayā vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: As that one honored by the worlds swiftly mounted the car, those horses, swift as the wind, at once bowed down their heads.

sanskrit: maheśvare tv āruhati jānubhyām agaman mahīm
english: And as Maheśvara ascended, they sank to the earth upon their knees.

sanskrit: abhīśūn hi trilokeśaḥ saṃgṛhya prapitāmahaḥ tān aśvāṃś codayām āsa manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: Then the great-grandsire, lord of the three worlds, taking up the reins, urged on those horses, swift as mind and as the wind.

sanskrit: tato 'dhirūḍhe varade prayāte cāsurān prati sādhu sādhv iti viśveśaḥ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Then, when the boon-giver had mounted and set forth against the asuras, the Lord of all, smiling, said: "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: yāhi deva yato daityāś codayāśvān atandritaḥ paśya bāhvor balaṃ me 'dya nighnataḥ śātravān raṇe
english: "Go, O God, where the Daityas are; urge on the horses, unwearied. Behold this day the strength of my arms as I strike down the foes in battle."
